summary: Released core mutual-information metric mixes scalar and joint densities, yielding exact nonzero/negative scores for constant representations and violating unused-coordinate invariance. Major is scoped to this metric; historical Figure5 binding unresolved. Alternative-regime summary has local contradictions. Main medium/high-budget accuracy trend survives.

problems.title: Released mutual-information score mixes scalar and vector densities
problems.claim: Section3.4/Figure5 use estimated I(X;Z) as a core explanatory metric for regime information flow and task suitability.
assumptions: All sampled representations equal a constant vector in R^d
d2 and supported sigma1 or.01; reference/evaluation samples arbitrary positive counts
Also inspect actual14-bandwidth average and both mc/jensen branches
Current public source revision, not certified historical Figure5 bytes
problems.check: Let c_sigma=log phi_sigma(0). Scalar log_post is c, joint log_prior is d*c, so score=(1-d)c. Appending an identically zero coordinate adds -c to any dataset's score while true information is unchanged.
problems.result: Constant d2 score.9189385332 at sigma1; -3.6862316528 at sigma.01; actual bandwidth mean1.4642039381. Constant d2000 mean2926.9436723553. Exact for all draws; not Monte Carlo variance.
problems.counterevidence: Kernel surrogate can be useful but needs valid target/derivation. Standard EE setup_mi is commented out and MI flagsfalse; no current-source-to-Figure5 run binding. No claim historical figure equals defective output or accuracy rankings fail.
problems.impact: Invalid released computation of a core analytical framework metric and its evidentiary route for compression/regime selection. Historical empirical effect Needs Evidence.
problems.correction: Fix dimensional term and specify noisy/quantized estimand. Report gives valid empirical Gaussian-channel expectation with noise sampled in both conditional/marginal evaluation; rerun analysis at justified bandwidth.
problems.repair_verification: Analytic constant-map and independent-coordinate identities checked; scalar factor alone not full repair, no repaired estimator run or Figure5 rerun.

problems.title: Alternative-regime comparisons overstate displayed results
problems.claim: AppendixA says alternating consistently underperforms both mixed/joint, and mixed-gradual outperforms mixed.
assumptions: Compare published means under same task/budget
Accuracy higher better, MSE lower better
problems.check: ViT-T CIFAR100100% alternating68.39>joint66.49; STSB100% alternatingMSE.50<joint.52 andmixed.51; Newsgr50/75/100 mixed-gradual81.35<mixed85.25.
problems.result: Unqualified comparative conclusions contradicted by displayed own results.
problems.counterevidence: Tables transparently display exceptions; mixed remains better than alternating in cited CIFAR cases, mixed-gradual helps other tasks; broad central qualified mixed recommendation remains supported.
problems.impact: Local comparative inference defect, no demonstrated reversal of central empirical pattern.
problems.correction: Qualify each comparison by task, budget and uncertainty.
problems.repair_verification: Metric directions and source table numbers checked against original renders and reviewer tally.
